name: Kathleen Roy
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember saving for a blazer in a biscuit jar.” On Thursday, near Breakwater Way, Kathleen stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I earned the uniform money washing hotel sheets. I sat down on the stairs before I could tell my boy.
appearance: Kathleen is easy to recognize by a smooth side part with one rebellious curl and a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Usually dressed in a dark green knitted vest with a thin silver ring worn on a cord, Kathleen presses the lips together to keep a smile in when listening.
personality: Kathleen is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Kathleen loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
agenda: To restore a dry set of school clothes by morning.
family: Hamish Mann is Kathleen’s cousin. Kathleen offers the first invitation. Hamish gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *A clean coat for court*, Hamish says, “I had planned to wait outside. Seeing the lender sit alone made me move one chair closer.”
connections: Lily Parra. A damaged shirt and a borrowed blazer form one usable first-day uniform.

reactions.situation: A student turns up in the wrong uniform
reactions.response: Kathleen gets the child through the gate before discussing the uniform with an adult.

reactions.situation: A friend asks for a loan due back before payday
reactions.response: Kathleen agrees on a sum and a date with the friend in private, keeping the arrangement out of family gossip.
